rationale: The Latin anchors *puer*, *juvenis*, and *adolescens* all point to the original sense of "knave" as a boy, youth, or male servant — not the modern pejorative "scoundrel" (rogue.n.01) nor the playing-card sense (jack.n.09). The OE *cnapa* in these biblical and monastic contexts means a young man or boy-servant, a sense that has no adequate WordNet analog among the offered candidates.
